Requirement: The mission shall support configuration A as one late-2028 precursor vehicle with three probes, and configuration B as two 2031 science vehicles with seven probes per vehicle.
Acceptance: Configuration inspection shall show 3 A probes or 14 B probes across two independent B vehicles; launch dates remain planning targets.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Use a common architecture with configuration-controlled bay counts and separate vehicle identities. Plan the late-2028 precursor as 1 vehicle with 3 probes and the 2031 mission as 2 vehicles with 7 probes each, for 14 probes total.

Requirement: The mission shall define and verify a host upper-stage mechanical, electrical, deployment-envelope and release-command interface before flight integration. Host selection shall remain provisional until interface and delivery agreements are approved.
Acceptance: Approved interface control document and host acceptance test shall close TBD-01; the host agreement shall identify the selected interface and delivery conditions.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map; see Appendix A for the phase and science-workflow allocation
Assumed solution: Use a keyed mechanical adapter and an isolated release-command interface defined in a host ICD. Start trade studies with a 28 V electrical interface, 2 independent release inhibits, and a single end-to-end host compatibility test before integration.

Requirement: Mission trajectory planning shall use a 400 km circular Mars-orbit initial reference for both default configurations and explicitly record off-default orbit trades.
Acceptance: Default capture shall report 400 km; mission analysis shall replace the reference with a host-provided state and covariance before release.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Initialize both designs from a 400 km circular Mars orbit and record the host state as 6 Cartesian components plus a 6 × 6 covariance. Use a 3–20 orbit targeting search as the initial planning window.

Requirement: The mission shall close the wet-mass budget at or below 20 kg per A vehicle and 50 kg per B vehicle, counting propulsion, nitrogen, all retained vehicles and reserves once.
Acceptance: Weighed flight configuration plus approved uncertainty shall meet the configuration limit; current proportional budgets are allocations, not weigh-test evidence.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Track wet mass once at the vehicle boundary, including loaded propulsion and nitrogen. Start with an A allocation of 19 kg plus 1 kg reserve and a B allocation of 47.5 kg plus 2.5 kg reserve against the respective 20 kg and 50 kg ceilings.

Requirement: The mission shall deliver independently operable probes and preserve sample location, acquisition depth, acquisition time and environmental provenance for each returned science record.
Acceptance: End-to-end deployment, acquisition and record-recovery test shall retain all required provenance fields for each functioning probe.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Give each probe an independent sample record with its vehicle and probe IDs, acquisition time, source coordinates, estimated depth and environmental measurements. Size an initial record for 1 s time resolution and 1 mm depth encoding, with separate uncertainty fields.

Requirement: The mission shall execute separation, attitude acquisition, retroburn, heat-shield alignment, module jettison, passive entry, cover release, carrier extraction, probe release, science acquisition and data return in a gated sequence.
Acceptance: State-transition tests shall show the specified delivery order including pre-entry alignment and module release interlocks; no downstream event shall bypass its required gate.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Use an event-gated mission controller with measured completion before every irreversible transition. Seed the trajectory with a 125 km entry interface, 10 km extraction reference, and first probe release at 5 km, followed by 2 s spacing.

Requirement: Each B vehicle and each released probe shall retain independent identity, mission state and failure reporting.
Acceptance: Fault injection into one vehicle or probe shall not falsify another vehicle or probe confirmation record.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Use immutable vehicle/probe identities and per-source event journals so a reset or missing packet affects only its own status. Allocate 8 bits each to vehicle and probe identifiers and 32 bits to the per-source event sequence.

Requirement: The mission shall establish an entry corridor, accepted attitude/rate envelope and verified module separation before authorizing entry readiness.
Acceptance: Six-degree-of-freedom dispersed trajectory and separation analysis shall close TBD-02 and TBD-03; animation orientation is not evidence.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Use a dispersed six-degree-of-freedom analysis and separation verification before arming entry readiness. Begin sensitivity runs with ±5° heat-shield pointing, a 2°/s rate ceiling and at least 30 s between confirmed jettison and the model entry interface.

Requirement: The mission shall obtain an approved orbiter relay service and RF interface before claiming a supported Earth-return path.
Acceptance: Relay-provider acceptance and end-to-end protocol test shall close TBD-04; a link-budget screen alone shall not constitute access approval.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Use buffered 400 MHz UHF proximity transmissions under an orbiter service agreement and confirm delivery through a relay acknowledgment or ground receipt. Begin the link screen at 400 km slant range, 10 W RF output and 3 dB receiver margin.

Requirement: The mission shall budget 24 hours of probe operations for A and 72 hours for B as the current design goals.
Acceptance: Measured power and selected assay schedule shall demonstrate the applicable duration or trigger a controlled requirement change; the proposed 1–5-sol assay duration remains an unresolved conflict.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Use a duty-cycled surface timeline with priority data return and an explicit energy reserve. Size for 24 h on A and 72 h on B, beginning with 20 Wh usable energy and reserving 4 Wh before scheduling experiment loads.

Requirement: The mission shall close all applicable flight requirements and departures before committing a vehicle to flight.
Acceptance: Verification matrix shall contain approved evidence and disposition for each applicable requirement; software model passes alone shall not close hardware verification.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Use a configuration-specific verification matrix with a named reviewer and evidence reference for every applicable requirement. Require 100% disposition of applicable rows and 0 unapproved departures before release for flight.

Requirement: The mission shall record the exact pitch filename, revision, slide numbering and checksum used for requirements allocation.
Acceptance: Verify the presentation configuration record against the approved phase allocation and close TBD-00.
Source: Current defaults; Rev09 mission family; recorded pitch phase map
Assumed solution: Place presentation artifacts under configuration control with a filename, revision identifier, numbered slides and SHA-256 checksum. Allocate 1 manifest entry per artifact, and use the 10-slide phase map as the initial trace structure.

Requirement: The probe sample-acquisition subsystem shall deliver a traceable sample to the selected experiment chamber and distinguish nose penetration, accessible source depth, recovered volume and recovered mass. If the sealed gas/trap option is selected, the design shall demonstrate the proposed 2–5 cm accessible source zone and 0.25 cubic centimetres per vessel; if the extraction option is selected, it shall demonstrate approximately 1 g recovered soil with an approved tolerance.
Acceptance: Measure source depth, volume, mass and recovery after representative impacts for the selected option; close TBD-05 and TBD-06. Do not equate nose depth with accessible source depth or convert volume to mass without measured density.
Source: Architecture probe-hardware-01; PRB-004, PRB-006, PRB-008; see Appendix A for the phase and science-workflow allocation
Assumed solution: Use a protected side intake with a depth fiducial and independent recovered-quantity measurement. Screen the sealed assay at 2–5 cm accessible source depth and 0.25 cm³ per vessel, or the extraction branch at 1.0 ± 0.2 g of recovered soil.

Requirement: The probe chamber and fluid subsystem shall isolate test, blank and control channels and contain the selected gases, liquids and reagents.
Acceptance: Leak, cross-contamination and recovery tests under the selected pressure/temperature envelope; close TBD-06.
Assumed solution: Use separate, positively isolated sample and control cartridges, each leak-tested before integration. Start with 3 independently isolated fluid paths and a qualification screen of ≤1% cross-channel carryover by a nonreactive tracer.

Requirement: The probe power subsystem shall provide regulated rails and peak-current capability through impact, acquisition, incubation, extraction and data return.
Acceptance: Load-profile test shall include heater, valves, SiPM bias and RF peaks plus an approved data-return reserve; close TBD-07.
Assumed solution: Use an impact-supported battery with separate logic, actuator and detector power branches plus regulated RF supply. Allocate 20 Wh usable, 4 Wh for data return and an illustrative 5 A transient capacity on the main bus.

Requirement: The probe environment-sensing subsystem shall record sample and detector temperatures, chamber pressure and hydration history with validity flags.
Acceptance: Calibrated sensor tests shall retain measured values, time and validity at the approved sample rate; close TBD-08.
Assumed solution: Install independent sample and detector temperature sensors, a chamber pressure sensor and a hydration proxy. Begin calibration at 1 Hz with ±0.5 °C temperature and ±0.1 kPa pressure targets, storing validity with each record.

Requirement: The probe detector subsystem shall measure scintillation signals with calibrated background, live time, temperature and bias dependence.
Acceptance: Calibration shall establish efficiency, saturation, dead time and isotope-response behavior for the selected geometry; close TBD-09.
Assumed solution: Use a solid-state scintillator coupled to a temperature-monitored SiPM with separately recorded bias and live time. Start electronics characterization with 1 s count bins and sweep a 10–10,000 counts/s reference range for linearity and saturation.

Requirement: The probe controller and storage subsystem shall retain raw science and health records across the specified impact, reset and power-interruption environments.
Acceptance: Impact and power-cycle tests shall recover committed records with identity, integrity checks and reset cause; close TBD-10.
Assumed solution: Use a mechanically supported microcontroller and nonvolatile storage with independent commit and recovery records. Allocate 60 MB on A and 252 MB on B to the probe-science portion of the logical budget per vehicle. Screen for complete recovery of committed records after 100 power interruptions.

Requirement: The probe shall include an independent drogue chute and a structural load path from canopy attachments to the impact-resistant probe body.
Acceptance: Opening-load, clearance and impact tests shall meet TBD-03; canopy reference diameter is 0.5 m, subject to qualification.
Assumed solution: Use a 0.50 m independent drogue with its loads carried by structural attachments on the probe body. Start opening and impact tests at a 500 N drag screening limit and a 1,500 g₀ shock screening level, pending measured loads.

Requirement: The probe thermal enclosure shall maintain the sample and detector within separately specified operating limits throughout the selected experiment.
Acceptance: Transient thermal-vacuum and experiment tests shall demonstrate each limit including heater energy; close TBD-07 and TBD-11.
Assumed solution: Thermally isolate the chamber and detector and monitor each with its own temperature channel. For the extraction concept, begin with a 0–5 °C sample range, a −10 to 30 °C detector housing range and a 1 W peak chamber heater allocation.

Requirement: The probe shall provide a self-contained antenna structure and RF feed that permit independent buffered science downlink after release and impact. The antenna and drogue shall be independent, with no connecting tether.
Acceptance: Post-impact RF tests in representative burial, canopy and antenna orientations shall demonstrate TBD-04 without relying on an unselected shroud-supported antenna geometry.
Source: Architecture probe-hardware-09; SYS-001, SYS-002, COM-01; see Appendix A for the phase and science-workflow allocation
Assumed solution: Use a body-mounted 400 MHz radiator and independent feed that remain attached after touchdown. Start with 10 W peak RF and test 3 antenna orientations over a 0–5 cm burial-depth range in representative material.

Requirement: Probe boot software shall record probe identity, firmware version, calibration identity, reset cause and a monotonic record-time origin.
Acceptance: Cold boot and reset tests shall populate each field and reject invalid configuration.
Assumed solution: At boot, verify a signed configuration and store probe ID, firmware and calibration revisions, reset cause and a hardware-counter origin. Begin with a 64-bit monotonic count in milliseconds and a 1 s boot self-test allocation.

Requirement: Probe health software shall inhibit experiment actuation when configured energy, containment or required-sensor validity gates are unsatisfied.
Acceptance: Inject each invalid gate and verify actuation is inhibited and the reason logged.
Assumed solution: Gate physical actuation on chamber status, sample-sensor validity and usable energy above the return reserve. Begin with a 4 Wh reserve and invalidate environmental samples more than 2 s old. Log each blocked transition with its reason.

Requirement: Probe power-management software shall schedule the selected assay within the measured energy budget while preserving the allocated data-return reserve.
Acceptance: Worst-case task-load tests shall produce a stop, pause or rejected schedule before the configured reserve is consumed.
Assumed solution: Use a task graph with measured energy costs and debit the reserve before authorizing another science task. Start with 60 s energy-accounting updates and a protected 4 Wh return budget in both configurations.

Requirement: Probe registry software shall associate every sample, control and extracted fraction with source channel, acquisition time, mass and processing history.
Acceptance: Trace test shall recover the association for every generated record, including rejected samples.
Assumed solution: Use a persistent registry that assigns every sample, control and fraction its own identifier and parent record. Start with 32-bit record IDs and 1 mg quantity encoding, storing acquisition time, source channel and the reason for any rejection.

Requirement: Probe assay software shall implement an explicit, reset-safe state machine for preparation, baseline, incubation, extraction and measurement.
Acceptance: Exercise valid transitions, illegal transitions, interruption and recovery without duplicate irreversible dosing.
Assumed solution: Implement explicit prepare, baseline, incubate, extract and measure states with a durable checkpoint before irreversible actuation. Budget 5 nominal states and 2 recovery outcomes, resume or inhibit, with a power-loss test at each transition.

Requirement: Probe acquisition software shall store raw counts or spectra together with sensor validity, live time, detector bias and detector temperature.
Acceptance: Known-signal tests shall recover raw data and acquisition metadata without treating invalid intervals as zero signal.
Assumed solution: Write raw counts together with live time, bias, detector temperature and data validity. Begin with 1 s count bins and 1 ms live-time resolution. Mark invalid intervals separately in the science record.

Requirement: Probe reduction software shall apply only identified calibration, blank and recovery corrections and retain their versions and uncertainties.
Acceptance: Reference datasets shall reproduce approved calculations; missing or ill-conditioned calibration shall result in qualified outputs, not an isotope estimate.
Assumed solution: Apply versioned calibration and blank/recovery corrections with an uncertainty field on each derived result. Flag isotope estimates with a response-matrix condition number above 10 or when any of the 3 correction records is absent.

Requirement: Probe storage software shall maintain a checksum-protected, reset-safe science journal and preserve raw records when derived products change.
Acceptance: Interrupted-write and bit-corruption tests shall distinguish committed, incomplete and corrupt records.
Assumed solution: Use an append-only journal with a length, sequence, CRC-32 and commit marker for every record. Start with a 4 KiB write block and retain the complete raw record after reprocessing or interrupted writes.

Requirement: Probe communication software shall identify and sequence science packets, queue unsent records and distinguish transmission attempts from confirmed delivery.
Acceptance: Loss, duplicate and out-of-order packet tests shall recover identity and sequence without falsely confirming reception.
Assumed solution: Queue labeled science frames for retry and keep attempted transmission separate from acknowledged delivery. Begin with 256-byte payloads, 32-bit sequence numbers and a nominal 1 s transmission opportunity every 60 s.

Requirement: The reentry module attitude sensors shall supply a validity-qualified estimate of orientation and angular rate for each controlled maneuver.
Acceptance: Sensor and estimator tests under the accepted environment shall meet TBD-02; simulated perfect attitude is not evidence.
Assumed solution: Fuse an optical attitude reference with a three-axis gyro and invalidate estimates when sources disagree. Begin hardware tests with 100 Hz inertial data, 5 Hz optical updates and a ±2° attitude-error target.

Requirement: The reentry module controller shall command propulsion and paired jets through independently inhibited actuator interfaces.
Acceptance: Hardware-in-the-loop tests shall demonstrate valid commands, inhibits, sensor fault responses and independent hardware ignition barriers.
Assumed solution: Separate the guidance processor from independently inhibited actuator switching and monitor commands on a distinct hardware-enable path. Begin with a 100 Hz control loop and a 100 ms watchdog timeout.

Requirement: The reentry module propulsion subsystem shall provide the configuration-specific retroburn with a thrust load path to the primary vehicle structure.
Acceptance: A reference is 100 N for 20 s and 2,000 N s at assumed Isp 225 s; B uses a 250 s Isp hybrid sizing model with 12.8 s burn. Selected motor curves and structural loads shall close TBD-12.
Assumed solution: Use a thrust ring that passes motor loads to the primary structure. Screen A with 100 N for 20 s, 2,000 N·s total impulse and 225 s assumed Isp; size B for a 12.8 s burn at 250 s assumed Isp.

Requirement: The reentry module shall provide a pressure vessel, regulator and plumbing compatible with 0.100 kg initial nitrogen at the reference 200 bar and 293 K.
Acceptance: Pressure-system design and tests shall establish the operating and qualification envelopes under TBD-13; the ideal-gas storage volume is a reference, not a tank drawing.
Assumed solution: Use a regulated nitrogen supply with pressure and temperature sensing. Start the ideal-gas sizing at 0.100 kg, 200 bar and 293 K, corresponding to about 0.435 L, with a 20 bar minimum regulation reference.

Requirement: The reentry module six-jet cold-gas subsystem shall retain separate gas allocations for upper-stage separation, retroburn alignment and heat-shield entry alignment.
Acceptance: Gas-accounting test shall show all three withdrawals, leakage and minimum-pressure reserve once, with no gas credited after jettison. Initial screening uses 0.1 N per jet, 0.25 m lever arm and 65 s Isp; qualify the selected jet geometry and performance under TBD-02 and TBD-13.
Assumed solution: Allocate six 0.10 N jets with a 0.25 m effective lever arm and 65 s assumed Isp. Keep separately metered budgets for 0.20 m/s separation, 90° burn alignment and 180° entry alignment.

Requirement: The reentry module shall provide independent ignition and jettison inhibits with release-state sensing.
Acceptance: Hardware barrier and fault-injection tests shall prevent premature ignition or jettison and close TBD-14.
Assumed solution: Use separate hardware arm and fire/release paths with independently reported states. Begin with 2 independent inhibits for each function and require zero unintended actions in single-fault injection.

Requirement: The reentry module power subsystem shall support propulsion control, sensing, actuators and handover through confirmed jettison.
Acceptance: Worst-case electrical load and disconnect testing shall maintain required functions until handover completes; close TBD-07.
Assumed solution: Use a separate module battery and an isolated handover harness. Take 12 Wh usable and a 20% reserve as initial power allocations and require a 5 s powered handover window after valid status transfer begins.

Requirement: The reentry module mechanical interface shall release all mechanical and electrical connections without damaging the retained capsule or extraction path.
Acceptance: Dispersed separation analysis and representative release tests shall demonstrate positive clearance and disconnected harnesses; close TBD-03. Verify thrust load transfer, motor heat isolation and plume/contamination clearance under TBD-11 and TBD-12.
Assumed solution: Use a restrained structural ring and positively separable electrical interface to keep motor loads and heat away from the retained capsule. Start the interface trade with a 1.5 load factor, 50 mm post-release clearance and separate thermal and plume screens.

Requirement: The reentry module status interface shall transfer measured burn, attitude, gas and release information to the retained mission avionics before loss of connection.
Acceptance: Handover test shall recover records with validity and confirmation source; command issuance shall not substitute for measured confirmation.
Assumed solution: Send a structured handover record with source ID, burn status, attitude, gas and release evidence. Begin with a 10 Hz status stream and 2 independently sensed release states, each timestamped by the retained controller.

Requirement: Reentry-module initialization software shall load the correct A/B configuration and validate sensor, actuator, clock and power readiness.
Acceptance: Wrong-configuration and invalid-sensor tests shall inhibit maneuver arming.
Assumed solution: Boot from a checksum-verified A or B configuration and hold actuators inhibited until host separation and sensor checks pass. Begin with a 100 ms heartbeat check and 2 independent separation indications.

Requirement: Reentry-module separation software shall perform the upper-stage clearance maneuver and verify the configured release conditions.
Acceptance: Test the 0.2 m/s reference separation impulse and 20 m clearance assumption with independent sensing criteria under TBD-03.
Assumed solution: Sequence the translation jets after sensed host release and estimate clearance from relative motion. Use 0.20 m/s commanded separation and a 20 m initial clearance gate, with positive release evidence before maneuvering.

Requirement: Reentry-module navigation and planning software shall estimate the vehicle state and identify an approved retroburn opportunity from mission navigation and target data.
Acceptance: Known-state and invalid-navigation tests shall distinguish a valid target opportunity from the website nearest-candidate screen; attitude/target tolerances and flight navigation authority shall close TBD-02.
Assumed solution: Propagate a 400 km starting orbit against the ephemeris and rank deorbit opportunities by ground-track residual. Search 3–20 orbits initially and screen against 100 km for A and 50 km for B, pending navigation and target validation.

Requirement: Reentry-module attitude software shall execute the retroburn-alignment maneuver within its accepted pointing and rate limits.
Acceptance: Evaluate the current 90-degree reference slew, saturation and gas demand in hardware-in-the-loop tests; close TBD-02.
Assumed solution: Use a closed-loop paired-jet maneuver to acquire burn attitude. Begin with a 90° reference slew and hold pointing within ±2° and rate within 1°/s for 1 s before authorizing ignition.

Requirement: Reentry-module burn software shall authorize, time and monitor the burn only after valid attitude, time and hardware-enable gates.
Acceptance: Gate-failure and interrupted-burn tests shall show inhibited ignition or defined fault response; delivered impulse requires motor evidence.
Assumed solution: Use explicit inhibited, armed, firing and completed states with measured thrust or acceleration to corroborate burn. Start time checks with 20 s for A, 12.8 s for B and a ±0.5 s diagnostic tolerance.

Requirement: Reentry-module entry-alignment software shall orient the heat shield for entry before module release.
Acceptance: Evaluate the current 180-degree reference slew and completion evidence; a changed mount shall require re-derived signed attitudes and gas budgets.
Assumed solution: Use a closed-loop postburn slew with persistence before enabling release. Start the assumed bottom-mount case with a 180° turn, ±5° pointing tolerance and 2°/s rate ceiling; rederive these values when mount geometry changes.

Requirement: Reentry-module fault software shall distinguish sensor invalidity, actuator nonresponse, incomplete burn and incomplete release and execute approved responses.
Acceptance: Fault injection shall exercise each state without generating false completion bits; close TBD-14 for approved responses.
Assumed solution: Separate sensor, actuator, burn and release faults in the supervisor and inhibit progression when completion is unconfirmed. Start with 4 fault classes, a 100 ms invalid-sensor timeout and a 2 s release-confirmation timeout.

Requirement: Reentry-module resource software shall account for separation, retroburn alignment and entry alignment gas independently and flag a reserve deficit.
Acceptance: Reference-vector tests shall close nitrogen mass and pressure accounting including leakage and minimum regulator pressure.
Assumed solution: Debit each maneuver independently and recompute usable mass above the regulator floor. Track 3 maneuver withdrawals plus leakage against the 0.100 kg loaded reference and flag a deficit at 20 bar.

Requirement: Reentry-module handover software shall commit confirmed mission state before jettison and remove authority over absent actuators after separation.
Acceptance: Disconnect tests shall preserve retained event history and reject post-jettison module actuator commands.
Assumed solution: Use positive acknowledgment of a retained state record before jettison, then invalidate the removed module’s actuator handles. Begin with 2 checked transaction records and a 5 s maximum handover interval.

Requirement: The capsule forebody shall use a 70-degree sphere-cone half-angle measured from the symmetry axis, equivalent to 20 degrees from the heat-shield plane.
Acceptance: CAD inspection shall verify the angle convention at a 0.8 m reference base diameter; nose/shoulder blend geometry and tolerances shall close TBD-15. The 0.745588 m total envelope is provisional packaging geometry.
Assumed solution: Use a preliminary 0.800 m sphere-cone aeroshell with a 70° half-angle from the symmetry axis. Carry a 0.200 m nose radius, 0.070 m shoulder radius and 0.746 m packaging height into the CAD and thermal trade.

Requirement: The capsule sensing subsystem shall provide validity-qualified entry acceleration and thermal records to the retained avionics.
Acceptance: Calibrated environmental sensor tests shall meet TBD-08 and preserve measurements through extraction handover.
Assumed solution: Use a calibrated entry accelerometer and center/shoulder temperature sensors read by retained avionics. Begin with 100 Hz acceleration and 10 Hz temperature acquisition, each with independent quality flags.

Requirement: The capsule restraint subsystem shall retain the loaded carrier during launch, burn and entry until commanded extraction.
Acceptance: Structural and release tests shall demonstrate the approved load envelope and release margin under TBD-03.
Assumed solution: Use a captive carrier cradle attached to the shell structure, with load-bearing mounts and independently sensed releases. Start with 4 restraints and a 1.5 preliminary ultimate-to-limit load factor for the structural trade.

Requirement: The capsule top-cover mechanism shall provide independent release inhibits and positive cover-clear evidence.
Acceptance: Latch, timeout, partial-release and obstructed-path tests shall prevent unconfirmed cover clearance from enabling extraction.
Assumed solution: Use a passively cleared cover with independent inhibits and positive open/clear sensors. Start with 2 independent clear indications and a 2 s timeout that prevents carrier extraction.

Requirement: The capsule mass distribution and aerodynamic configuration shall meet approved static and dynamic stability criteria over the complete entry envelope.
Acceptance: Obtain Mach/angle-dependent coefficients, damping, as-built CG/inertia and dispersed six-degree-of-freedom results; close TBD-02. The website 0.19D illustrative bound is not a flight CG limit.
Assumed solution: Model passive entry with an as-built mass-properties survey and Mach-dependent force/moment tables. Start with CG at 0.15D and a 0.05D static-margin screen, then test the scenario in dispersed 6-DOF runs.

Requirement: The capsule extraction-chute interface shall transfer opening loads and extract the loaded carrier through a demonstrated clear path.
Acceptance: Representative extraction tests shall verify opening loads, cover clearance and carrier separation under TBD-03.
Assumed solution: Connect the extraction chute load path to the retained carrier cradle and keep it clear of the cover mechanism. Screen the 1.5 m A and 2.0 m B canopies at a 600 Pa extraction-pressure ceiling.

Requirement: The capsule retro attachment shall connect to a verified structural load path and leave a qualified retained entry surface after module release.
Acceptance: Demonstrate structure, thermal continuity and separation for the selected mount; top-side bridge preference remains an unselected trade under TBD-16.
Assumed solution: Trade a guarded structural bridge against forebody attachment with a restored uninterrupted TPS surface. Start CAD with a 1.5 load factor and 50 mm separation-clearance screen for each mounting option.

Requirement: The capsule power and event interface shall maintain event continuity across retro release and carrier extraction without duplicated avionics mass credit.
Acceptance: Interface test shall verify time, state and power continuity with execution ownership closed under TBD-17.
Assumed solution: Run the entry data interface from retained carrier power through a separable harness. Begin with a nominal 28 V link, 5 s handover buffer and 2 source IDs identifying module and retained avionics.

Requirement: The capsule discard configuration shall clear the extracted carrier and released probes without crediting further capsule control or telemetry.
Acceptance: Dispersed discard-clearance study and representative separation test shall close TBD-03.
Assumed solution: Use passive separation guides to send the discard body outside the carrier path. Start the dispersion screen at ≥1 m relative clearance within 2 s, and verify lack of recontact through the first probe release.

Requirement: Capsule handover software shall accept retro status only with source identity, validity, time continuity and module-detached evidence.
Acceptance: Test lost, corrupt and inconsistent handover records and verify readiness remains unconfirmed.
Assumed solution: Decode and validate the retro handover record before entering the passive-entry state. Use a CRC-32, a 2 s freshness window and 2 consistent detached indications as initial checks.

Requirement: Capsule monitoring software shall time-tag available acceleration and thermal measurements and their validity throughout entry.
Acceptance: Replay calibrated and failed-sensor data and verify records remain distinguishable from estimated values.
Assumed solution: Record acceleration and temperature as separate data streams with a shared monotonic time and validity bits. Start with 100 Hz acceleration, 10 Hz thermal recording and 1 ms timestamp encoding.

Requirement: Capsule phase-estimation software shall determine deployment readiness from approved physical sensor/state gates.
Acceptance: Replay dispersed trajectories and sensor faults; animation progress or compressed review time shall never trigger deployment.
Assumed solution: Use a filtered entry phase estimator with physical altitude and pressure as independent deployment cues. Begin with a 10 km extraction reference, 600 Pa pressure ceiling and 1 s valid-state persistence.

Requirement: Capsule deployment software shall inhibit cover and extraction actuation outside the approved deployment envelope or without required readiness gates.
Acceptance: Boundary and fault tests shall exercise each gate and independent hardware barrier; close TBD-18.
Assumed solution: Keep cover and extraction outputs inhibited until the measured deployment envelope and independent enables are true. Start boundary testing at a 10 km altitude reference, 600 Pa pressure ceiling and 2 separate hardware permits.

Requirement: Capsule cover-release software shall command release, await measured clearance and execute an approved timeout response.
Acceptance: Partial-release and no-response tests shall not advance extraction state without required confirmation.
Assumed solution: Command the cover only once after all permits are valid and wait for confirmed clearance. Use 2 agreeing switches and a 2 s confirmation timeout that holds extraction inhibited.

Requirement: Capsule extraction software shall command carrier extraction only after cover clearance and shall record carrier-separation confirmation.
Acceptance: Test nominal and failed extraction without conflicting actuation or false separation bits.
Assumed solution: Arm carrier extraction after the cover-clear checks, then record measured separation in the shared journal. Begin with a 1 s minimum delay after confirmed cover clearance and a 3 s separation timeout.

Requirement: Capsule diagnostic software shall preserve command, measurement, confirmation and fault histories for transfer to the retained carrier.
Acceptance: Disconnect and reset tests shall retain all committed upstream events and source identities.
Assumed solution: Journal commands, measurements, confirmations and faults using immutable per-source sequence numbers. Budget 4 distinct record types and a 30 s ring buffer before handover.

Requirement: Capsule software allocation shall identify the processor, power source and authority for each entry and extraction function.
Acceptance: Architecture review shall close TBD-17; no dedicated capsule computer shall be assumed without an explicit mass/power allocation.
Assumed solution: Allocate entry and extraction functions to the retained carrier processor until discard and keep a single authority for each actuator. Use 1 active owner per function and a 5 s design handover window.

Requirement: Capsule end-of-service software shall mark capsule discard and cease credit for further capsule measurements or actuator availability.
Acceptance: Replay shall show carrier/probe independence after discard and no post-discard capsule telemetry claims.
Assumed solution: Mark discard only after sensing carrier separation, then invalidate the capsule data stream in retained avionics. Begin with 1 terminal capsule record and 0 valid capsule measurements credited after the discard event.

Requirement: The carrier frame shall accommodate three A probe bays or seven B probe bays with restraints and accessible release paths.
Acceptance: Fit and mass-property inspection plus load test shall meet TBD-03; reference retained dry masses are the derived A allocation and 8 kg for B.
Assumed solution: Use a common carrier frame with configuration-specific bay inserts and protected release paths. Allocate 3 bays and about 3 kg retained dry mass to A, and 7 bays and 8 kg retained dry mass to B.

Requirement: Each carrier probe-release mechanism shall have a defined actuation and positive release-sensing path.
Acceptance: Release tests shall distinguish commanded, partial, failed and completed drops and prevent adjacent probe contact.
Assumed solution: Equip each bay with a controlled release latch and independent open and bay-clear indications. Start with 2 confirmations per bay and a 2 s release verification window.

Requirement: The carrier parachute and risers shall support extraction and descent of the loaded carrier in the approved envelope.
Acceptance: Opening-load and descent tests shall qualify the 1.5 m A / 2.0 m B reference canopy diameters or control a design change; close TBD-03.
Assumed solution: Use reinforced risers and a qualified carrier canopy sized for each retained carrier. Start with diameters of 1.5 m for A and 2.0 m for B and a 1.5 opening-load factor for structural screening.

Requirement: The carrier shall estimate release altitude and descent state with validity sufficient for the selected release sequence.
Acceptance: Sensor and estimator tests shall demonstrate TBD-08 and TBD-18; the 5 km release reference shall not imply a qualified threshold.
Assumed solution: Fuse a descent pressure/altitude proxy with inertial and ground-range measurements where valid. Begin with a 5 km release reference, 10 Hz estimator updates and ±100 m initial altitude accuracy.

Requirement: The carrier avionics shall retain upstream event history and independently latched probe-drop confirmations through descent and reset.
Acceptance: Reset and interrupted-write tests shall preserve committed confirmations without clearing cumulative history.
Assumed solution: Give the carrier a dedicated controller and nonvolatile append-only event storage. Start with 4 MB of carrier event storage and verify all committed drop states survive 100 power-cycle or interrupted-write tests.

Requirement: The carrier radio and antenna subsystem shall transmit identifiable cumulative mission status independently of probe science transmissions.
Acceptance: RF and framing tests shall verify source identity, status mapping and TBD-04 relay compatibility.
Assumed solution: Use a separate 400 MHz carrier radio and antenna with a dedicated source ID. Size the initial status mode for a 1 s burst every 60 s at up to 10 W RF, subject to relay acceptance.

Requirement: The carrier power subsystem shall supply descent, release actuation, recording and repeated status transmissions with reserve.
Acceptance: Measured load-profile test shall close TBD-07; probe battery allocations shall not be substituted for carrier energy.
Assumed solution: Use an independent carrier battery and buffer sized for descent, release and status transmission. Start with 15 Wh usable, a 3 Wh reserve, and a separate 4 MB event queue.

Requirement: The carrier harness and separation interfaces shall disconnect safely from the capsule and each released probe while preserving required state.
Acceptance: Representative disconnect tests shall demonstrate no retained hazardous connections and correct post-release power/data ownership.
Assumed solution: Use keyed breakaway harnesses with independent current limiting and state confirmation at each disconnect. Start with contacts that indicate separation within 100 ms and verify electrical isolation for each of the 3 or 7 probe bays.

Requirement: The carrier probe interfaces shall permit each released probe to continue power, sensing, science control, storage and communications independently.
Acceptance: Representative release/disconnect tests shall verify no required carrier power or command dependence after release; probe impact survival remains separate under TBD-03.
Assumed solution: Release probes as self-contained instrument packages with individual drogues, power and antenna structures. Use 2 s nominal spacing and a separate 0.50 m drogue for each released probe.

Requirement: Carrier initialization software shall restore transferred mission history, configuration and vehicle identity before independent descent.
Acceptance: Handover and reset tests shall recover valid state and reject invalid or mismatched configuration.
Assumed solution: Restore the upstream journal only after verifying the vehicle identity, boot epoch and configuration. Check a CRC-32 on each record and test both bay layouts, 3 for A and 7 for B.

Requirement: Carrier descent software shall estimate altitude and release readiness with explicit sensor validity.
Acceptance: Dispersed descent and invalid-sensor tests shall inhibit drops outside the approved envelope under TBD-18.
Assumed solution: Run a quality-gated altitude and descent-state estimator. Start at 10 Hz, mark data stale after 2 s, and require valid descent through 5 km before authorizing the first release.

Requirement: Carrier release scheduling software shall release probes in the approved order and separation cadence.
Acceptance: Evaluate the default 5 km release altitude and 2 s cadence with collision/dispersion testing; close TBD-03 and TBD-18.
Assumed solution: Schedule releases individually, retaining bay identity and requiring independent confirmation before moving to the next bay. Start with 2 s cadence and run collision sensitivity for both the 3-bay and 7-bay configurations.

Requirement: Carrier event software shall latch the core mission confirmations and each applicable probe-drop event without clearing prior confirmations.
Acceptance: Packet mapping tests shall reproduce 9 A core bits and the 13-position B map while marking unused A positions not applicable.
Assumed solution: Use an append-only record and a cumulative status word with independent latched states. Begin with the 9-bit A and 13-bit B reference words and verify that a retransmission preserves all previously confirmed bits.

Requirement: Carrier confirmation software shall retain time-tagged command, sensed-drop and fault evidence for each probe bay.
Acceptance: Reset, stuck-actuator and duplicate-command tests shall preserve prior confirmations and distinguish failed or unknown release from a measured drop.
Assumed solution: Record command, partial release, confirmation and fault as 4 distinct evidence states. Use a CRC-32 on each journal record and test the reported state after a reset inserted at each transition.

Requirement: Carrier telemetry software shall frame the cumulative status with identity, time, integrity and sequence information.
Acceptance: Decode reference packets and corrupted packets; payload bits shall be distinguished from packet overhead.
Assumed solution: Use independent frame sequencing with retry and duplicate suppression by carrier ID. Start with 32-bit packet sequences and 3 retry opportunities per queued priority frame.

Requirement: Carrier resource software shall schedule release and repeated status transmissions within the carrier energy and storage budget.
Acceptance: Worst-case queue and energy tests shall preserve safety-critical records and configured reserve.
Assumed solution: Reserve energy and storage for high-priority fault and release records before lower-priority telemetry. Start at a 3 Wh energy floor and issue high-buffer alerts at 80% occupancy.

Requirement: Carrier contact-policy software shall buffer status through relay blackout and retry only within the approved access and energy policy.
Acceptance: Loss-of-contact, restored-contact and low-energy tests shall preserve queued records without claiming reception; close TBD-04 and TBD-07.
Assumed solution: Use predicted contact and queue priority to decide when to retry or buffer status. Begin with 60 s checks and an illustrative 30 min blackout test with no premature delivery confirmation.

Requirement: Carrier surface-status software shall manage repeated status reporting and actuator safing if the carrier remains operational after descent.
Acceptance: Ground/contact, timeout and energy-depletion tests shall verify the approved terminal policy under TBD-14; neither carrier survival nor surface RF coverage is assumed.
Assumed solution: On sensed terminal contact, inhibit unreleased bays and transmit terminal status until timeout or reserve cutoff. Start with 3 consecutive contact samples, a 15 min status window and a 3 Wh reserve floor.

Requirement: The system mass ledger shall distinguish wet mass, consumed propellant, gas withdrawals, jettisoned mass and retained entry mass at each mission boundary.
Acceptance: Mass-conservation review and test vectors shall balance each boundary without duplicated propulsion or carrier mass.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Track a single ledger with separate columns for wet mass, retro propellant used, each nitrogen withdrawal, discarded hardware and retained entry mass. Audit every event boundary to 0.01 kg and verify initial closure against 20 kg for A and 50 kg for B.

Requirement: The A mass ledger shall derive probe and carrier allocations from the current propulsion replacement and proportional non-propulsion scaling formula.
Acceptance: At default settings verify 0.906414 kg motor propellant, 0.100 kg nitrogen, 1.5 kg assumed motor/module dry mass, 1.999267 kg per probe and 2.998900 kg retained carrier dry allocation.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Replace the A propulsion allocation with 0.906414 kg motor propellant, 0.100 kg nitrogen and 1.500 kg dry module. Scale the remaining components by the available mass divided by the 17.5 kg reference nonpropulsion allocation, yielding about 1.999267 kg per probe and 2.998900 kg retained carrier dry mass at 20 kg.

Requirement: The reference link budget shall explicitly identify the 400 MHz, 400 km, 10 W RF, 0 dBi transmitter gain, 6 dBi receiver gain, 6 dB losses and −120 dBm receiver-threshold assumptions.
Acceptance: Reproduce link calculations in SI/dB units; antenna deployment and orbiter access require independent evidence under TBD-04.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Use a traceable free-space link budget and repeat it with measured antenna and relay data. Seed it with 400 MHz, 400 km, 10 W RF, 0 dBi transmit gain, 6 dBi receive gain, 6 dB losses and a −120 dBm receive threshold. Screen candidates for 3 dB margin.

Requirement: The probe power budget shall distinguish the 20 Wh usable-energy assumption, 0.2 W average-load assumption and 1 s transmission burst per 60 s from validated science load measurements.
Acceptance: Measured experiment and communication profile shall close TBD-07; a mean-load arithmetic endurance estimate shall not establish assay readiness.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Track usable energy, peak current and return reserves separately for each vehicle. Seed the probe calculation with 20 Wh usable, a 0.2 W average-load reference and a 1 s transmission burst per 60 s. With 4 Wh reserved, the remaining average allowances are about 0.67 W over 24 h and 0.22 W over 72 h.

Requirement: The carrier data architecture shall allocate the reference 64 MB A and 256 MB B buffers explicitly to packet and science storage owners.
Acceptance: Worst-case data-volume and write-rate test shall close TBD-19; source buffer values are not automatically installed probe memory.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Split the 64 MB A and 256 MB B reference data budgets per vehicle between the carrier packet/event queue and the released probes. Start with 4 MB for carrier events and packets and 60 MB for A or 252 MB for B probe science in aggregate, with 20% headroom inside each allocation. Validate overhead and write rate before rounding to installed capacities.

Requirement: The capsule TPS design shall meet selected material, bondline and residual-thickness criteria under a dispersed heating/pressure history through the relevant exposure and soak interval.
Acceptance: Material-response/ablation analysis and arc-jet testing shall close TBD-11; the 15 mm flight-model input and 60 mm illustrative sweep result shall not constitute a released thickness.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Use a two-location thermal model with explicit thickness, material and soak assumptions, then correlate it against material tests. Compare the 15 mm live reference with a 60 mm trade candidate under 1.5× heating and 300 s soak.

Requirement: The penetration design shall distinguish predicted nose depth, accessible sample depth and post-impact instrument operation.
Acceptance: Instrumented material tests correlated to a site/material envelope shall close TBD-05; uncalibrated Poncelet results and three-sigma shading shall not be treated as measured scatter.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Correlate penetration and shock predictions with instrumented material tests and measured accessible sample recovery. Start with 3 representative media, a 50–100 m/s impact-speed sweep and a separate 2–5 cm accessible-depth target.

Requirement: Each mechanical, power, data and command boundary among reentry module, capsule, carrier and probe shall have one accountable owner and an interface control record.
Acceptance: For every architecture edge, identify units, connector/release state, time origin, ownership and fault behavior; close TBD-17.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Assign processor, power source, data ownership and actuator authority for each interface and handover. Require 1 named owner per function and exercise 2 handovers, retro to retained avionics and capsule functions to independent carrier operations.

Requirement: Flight software shall use versioned configuration and calibration records with range checks and explicit A/B applicability.
Acceptance: Invalid, stale or cross-configuration records shall be rejected or safely qualified; test each irreversible-actuation gate.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Sign the configuration manifest with build and calibration identifiers and store it with every mission data export. Use SHA-256 for file identity, 2 software slots for recovery and a 32-bit configuration ID in the telemetry schema.

Requirement: Flight software shall represent commanded, measured, estimated, inferred, unknown and failed states distinctly.
Acceptance: Fault tests shall never turn a transmitted command or animation event into measured release, burn or science confirmation.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Use a six-state evidence field that distinguishes commanded, measured, estimated, inferred, unknown and failed. Keep relay receipt separate and inject at least 1 fault per state, with 0 confirmation bits set by command issuance alone.

Requirement: Flight software shall maintain consistent event time and reset provenance across all retained vehicle handovers.
Acceptance: Clock discontinuity, rollover and reset tests shall preserve event ordering or mark uncertainty under TBD-20.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Use a per-source monotonic counter and a boot epoch, with time-sync uncertainty stored separately. Begin with millisecond ticks, a 60 s resync interval and a 10 ms two-clock ordering-error screen.

Requirement: Mission data products shall preserve raw values, units, source vehicle, configuration, time, calibration version and quality flags.
Acceptance: End-to-end known-record tests shall verify transport integrity and prevent silent replacement of missing measurements with zero.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Wrap raw measurements in a versioned schema with source identity, unit, time, calibration ID and quality flags. Start with CRC-32 framing and exercise 3 explicit quality states: valid, missing and invalid.

Requirement: Flight software releases shall have reviewed requirements traceability, unit/integration testing, hardware-in-the-loop testing and controlled release records.
Acceptance: Every implemented safety or science-critical requirement shall link to its test and software build; unresolved anomalies require disposition.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Test nominal, boundary, reset and fault paths in software and on representative electronics. Plan 100% coverage of safety-relevant transitions and at least 1 hardware test for every independent inhibit.

Requirement: Engineering analyses shall record inputs, units, source revision, solver version, assumptions and validity limits for each output. Mission software and verification shall use physical time and approved event gates rather than animation or compressed presentation-event durations.
Acceptance: Reproduce website defaults and exports from the source fingerprint; test time/event mappings and distinguish numerical agreement, illustrative playback and physical validation.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces; see Appendix A for the phase and science-workflow allocation
Assumed solution: Version models, settings and inputs and export a reproducible physical event timeline. Record a SHA-256 source fingerprint, store time in seconds and compare selected numeric outputs against a 1% reproducibility tolerance.

Requirement: The integrated system shall define safe/abort responses to failed separation, incomplete burn, missed deployment gates, power deficit and data corruption.
Acceptance: An approved fault tree and hardware-in-the-loop campaign shall close TBD-14; timeout duration and fallback behavior shall not be improvised at flight time.
Source: Website defaults, calculation model and architecture interfaces
Assumed solution: Use a fault tree and an exercised response for every critical actuator and handover. Start with a 100 ms invalid-data timeout and a 2 s release timeout, checking for 0 false completion records across the fault campaign.

Requirement: The science design shall select and configuration-control its experiment suite before assay integration. The sealed gas/trap assay and incubation/extraction assay shall remain separate alternatives with independently defined conditions.
Acceptance: Record the selected workflow, sample quantity, channels, fluids, controls and detector method under TBD-00 and TBD-06.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4; see Appendix A for the phase and science-workflow allocation
Assumed solution: Carry the sealed assay and incubation/extraction assay as 2 separate configuration-controlled candidates until review. Use the existing 0.25 cm³ per vessel and approximately 1 g soil references to size their separate sample paths.

Requirement: The selected assay shall include time-zero, reagent/no-soil, matrix, killed and recovery controls capable of distinguishing specified abiotic alternatives.
Acceptance: Blinded terrestrial and simulant campaigns shall quantify false detections and recovery under TBD-09; retained radiolabel alone shall not constitute life detection.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4
Assumed solution: Design a blinded control panel for time-zero, reagent-only, matched matrix, inactivated reference and recovery controls. Start with 5 control classes and 3 replicate pairs per condition for preflight characterization.

Requirement: The selected experiment shall measure and record temperature, pressure, hydration history and relevant water-activity conditions. If the sealed gas/trap option is selected, the controlled reference procedure shall specify no added water, sealed and dark incubation at -10 to 0 degrees C for 1–5 sols. If the incubation/extraction option is selected, it shall specify near-Mars-ambient pressure and proposed 0–5 degrees C incubation, with fluid additions identified by process step.
Acceptance: Validate the selected condition envelope, tolerance and sensor capability under TBD-06 and TBD-08. Qualification shall document the selected condition envelope and method-specific limits.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4; see Appendix A for the phase and science-workflow allocation
Assumed solution: Measure and log chamber temperature, pressure and hydration history with each science record. Screen distinct environmental envelopes of −10 to 0 °C for the sealed concept and 0–5 °C for the extraction concept, beginning with 1 Hz logging.

Requirement: The radiotracer experiment shall account for initial and recovered isotope activity in gas, liquid, solid and loss fractions.
Acceptance: Calibrated recovery and isotope-exchange controls shall close TBD-09; unlabeled nutrients and exchangeable tritium shall be identified.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4
Assumed solution: Use a measurement ledger separating input activity, recovered gas, liquid and solid activity, and estimated losses. Start with 4 accounting categories after dosing and an illustrative 80–120% closure band to flag unexplained losses during ground controls.

Requirement: Any tritium/carbon-14 separation claim shall use a calibrated, identifiable response matrix and propagate its uncertainty.
Acceptance: Mixed-isotope and matrix tests shall demonstrate efficiency and cross-talk limits under TBD-09; photon-burst size alone is not sufficient.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4
Assumed solution: Use a calibrated two-channel response model with uncertainty propagation and explicit cross-talk controls. Start with a 2 × 2 response matrix, 3 reference mixtures and a condition-number screening limit of 10.

Requirement: The science measurement plan shall predeclare blank thresholds, detection/quantification limits, replicate counts and false-positive/false-negative decision criteria.
Acceptance: Blind controls and spiked samples shall meet TBD-09 before a detection-performance claim.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4
Assumed solution: Predeclare decision thresholds and use independently characterized blanks and positive references to validate sensitivity. Begin with 20 blank runs, 3 replicate pairs per condition and an illustrative 5% false-positive ceiling.

Requirement: The selected science workflow shall reconcile sample handling, incubation duration, detector, valve and heater loads and data-return reserve to the vehicle resource budget before selection. A 1–5-sol gas/trap procedure shall not be credited within the 24-hour A or 72-hour B operation goals unless an approved revised procedure or resource allocation demonstrates closure.
Acceptance: Test the selected end-to-end schedule and measured energy profile under TBD-07; record any changed incubation endpoint and its scientific validity. Do not substitute compressed playback duration for physical assay duration.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4; see Appendix A for the phase and science-workflow allocation
Assumed solution: Build separate battery and activity timelines for both science concepts, including detector, valves, heaters and relay reserve. Start with 24 h on A, 72 h on B and 4 Wh reserved for return. Treat the 1–5-sol sealed concept as an unresolved schedule trade.

Requirement: The probe shall return measurements and qualified analysis products rather than an unqualified autonomous life/no-life verdict.
Acceptance: Review packet schema and classification logic; negative measurements shall retain environmental and sensitivity limitations.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4
Assumed solution: Transmit the raw measurement and qualified analysis together with uncertainty and context fields. Start with 3 interpretation flags: below decision threshold, above threshold pending review, and invalid.

Requirement: The payload shall define containment, cleanliness and carryover limits for all selected reagents and sample-contacting materials.
Acceptance: Contamination budget, compatibility and cross-channel tests shall close TBD-06 before experiment integration.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4
Assumed solution: Use separate sealed sample and control paths with preflight cleanliness and compatibility verification. Begin with 3 isolated flow paths and an illustrative ≤1% carryover limit using an inert witness tracer.

Requirement: Any oxidant-screen experiment shall identify the product/selectivity controls needed to distinguish molecular oxygen, peroxide and superoxide interpretations.
Acceptance: Interferent and positive/negative-control tests shall close TBD-09; a nonspecific color or fluorescence change shall not uniquely identify a species.
Source: Benner supplied outline 2026-11-12; scientific review; recorded pitch slides 3–4
Assumed solution: Compare candidate optical channels against known reference materials and matrix interferents before drawing a selectivity conclusion. Start with 3 target-species reference classes, 3 replicate pairs per class and a 5% false-positive screening target.
